title: an authored path into the compiler's own emitted prelude is an ordinary untrusted foreign module edge
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Compiler Lifting' (Locked): "Authors MUST NOT need to write `Result.ok(...)` or `Result.err(...)`. Those constructors MUST NOT be part of the ordinary Smithers authoring API" — a Result the compiler did not construct at a checked exit has a failure channel that means nothing. specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Runtime TypeScript Dependency' (Locked) supplies the code: `__smithers_prelude.ts` is a `.ts` module under the project root carrying no leading `@module`/`@throws {never}` claim, so an author's path into it is exactly the untrusted foreign module edge SMITHERS1510 already owns. This case is deliberately about the PATH and nothing else: `Panic` is a sanctioned binding an author may legitimately import from `smithers:exceptions`, so the only thing the refusal can be about is the specifier. Splitting it that way is what makes it writable on both backends at one code and one position — see COVERAGE.md, 'Two prelude-constructor routes the corpus cannot express', for the two neighbouring routes that are NOT writable, and why. The Go fork ACCEPTED this program until 2026-08-25 with zero diagnostics: `isCompilerModuleSpecifier` resolves by module SYMBOL, which is the right question for deciding what the lowering must rewrite and the wrong one for deciding whether an author may name the compiler's own emitted file. The reference reaches the same code by a different branch — no such file exists in a reference project, so its message is the unresolved-module one. NO `messageContains` IS DECLARED HERE, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because this is exactly the shape of case a later lane would add one to. The two messages are: reference — "foreign module initialization can panic before a checked call boundary; './__smithers_prelude.ts' could not be resolved to a module carrying a leading JSDoc containing both @module and @throws {never}; …"; fork — "statically loaded TypeScript/JavaScript module does not declare a leading @module and @throws {never} initialization trust claim". The fragment that would carry THIS case's promise is the specifier, and only one backend prints it. The only fragment the two share is `@module and @throws {never}`, which names the rule rather than the payload — and conformance/README.md forbids that use outright ("declare `messageContains` only where the payload is the promise, and never as a way of naming the rule"). It is the right fragment for 09-foreign-calls/miscased-trust-markers-do-not-confer-module-trust, whose subject IS the marker's spelling, and the wrong one here, whose subject is the path. 01-result-lifting/the-compiler-owned-modules-still-serve-their-authoring-surface is the over-correction guard, and 01-result-lifting/a-star-re-export-of-the-compiler-owned-prelude-is-refused is the spelling that names no binding at all.
